title: Measured report register: weekday visits
instructions: Choose the option that expresses the intended meaning, forms a natural word partnership and fits the situation.

parts.prompt: In its annual report, the library states: ‘The number of weekday visits ___ from 420 to 510.’

choice_rationales.A: Shot up is conversational and suggests a dramatic rise; the report only states a measured change.
choice_rationales.B: Got bigger is informal and imprecise for a count reported with exact figures.
choice_rationales.C: Increased is neutral-formal, combines naturally with ‘from ... to ...’ and makes no unsupported claim about drama.
choice_rationales.D: Took off is informal and figurative, usually implying rapid success or movement beyond the stated figures.

parts.hint: Use the annual-report setting and choose the measured verb that works naturally with ‘from ... to ...’.
parts.correct_explanation: ‘Increased from 420 to 510’ is precise, natural and appropriately neutral-formal for an annual report.
